newsitem.title: ITALY: Slowdown in Italian GDP not worrying - Treasury.
newsitem.headline: Slowdown in Italian GDP not worrying - Treasury.

text.p: A slowdown in the Italian economy in the second quarter of 1996 was in line with government economic forecasts and not worrying, a Treasury official told Reuters.

Provisional data released by statistics office Istat on Friday, showed Italy's gross domestic product (GDP) falling 0.5 percent between April and June compared with the first quarter. On a year-over-year basis, the economy grew 0.5 percent.
The Treasury official said the figures were compatible with target growth of around 1.0 percent for all of 1996. "A lot will depend on the second-half economic trend," he said.
"GDP figures for the second quarter of 1996 went as expected and do not give cause for alarm," the source told Reuters.
The government's official forecast is for 1996 GDP growth of 1.2 percent.

However, employers' federation Confindustria said in a statement that Friday's data pointed to a stagnating economy. "It confirms our forecasts of 1996 growth well below one percent," the statement said.
"And at the start of this autumn, there is no sign of a pick-up," it added. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
